gap: The section repeatedly tells learners to 'read the markup, not the preview' and verify structure, alt text, and the cascade by reading source, but never names the free authoritative tools that automate these checks: the W3C Markup Validation Service for valid HTML and a browser accessibility audit (Lighthouse in Chrome/Edge DevTools, or axe DevTools) for missing alt text. Naming them turns the Decision Rule's three checks into a reproducible, evidence-producing workflow that fits the course's evidence-grounding value and feeds the Artifact Studio before/after requirement.
proposed_change: Add a short callout after the '## Decision Rule' three-check list (after line 90): 'You do not have to catch every issue by eye. Treat their reports as evidence in your revision trace.' IMPORTANT scoping correction grounded in the sources: phrase it as flagging MISSING alt (the automated image-alt rule), not judging alt quality, because Lighthouse/axe (axe-core) detect a missing/empty alt attribute but cannot evaluate whether the alt text is meaningful, and automated tools catch only ~30-40% of WCAG issues. proposed_change: In the '## Core Concept' Accessible images paragraph (line 30), anchor the WCAG link to the specific criterion: '...treat missing alt text on informative images as a failure of WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.1.1 (Non-text Content) (a Level A criterion), which is why this is not optional polish.' VERIFIED: WCAG 2.2 is the current W3C Recommendation (originally published 5 Oct 2023; current republished version dated 12 Dec 2024) and SC 1.1.1 'Non-text Content' (Level A) is unchanged from WCAG 2.0/2.1 -- it requires a text alternative for all non-text content, the normative basis for image alt text. sources.finding: MDN: 'Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) is an HTTP-header based mechanism that allows a server to indicate any origins (domain, scheme, or port) other than its own from which a browser should permit loading resources.' An origin is defined by scheme+domain+port; same-origin requests (e.g., a relative-path resource on the same site) are not subject to CORS. Confirms a same-folder/relative-path image is same-origin and CORS cannot apply.
